text: 23-year-old female. The patient presents with knee pain that started yesterday and has been steadily worsening. speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like a classic injury pattern for a 23-year-old active female; specifically, does the pain localize to the inner aspect of the knee or the front, and is there any audible "pop" or feeling of instability when you try to pivot?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Knee pain, specifically over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella. I also have Recent weight loss attempt, Increased physical activity.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pain location over the medial tibia sounds very specific; have you noticed any swelling, tenderness to the touch, or difficulty fully straightening your leg compared to the other side? Also, did you experience any audible "pop" or sudden instability during the volleyball activity?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS), currently managed with oral contraceptive pills. Social history: Has recently joined a volleyball team.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Medial Tibial Stress Syndrome (Shin Splains).

I have completed my assessment; the combination of medial tibial pain, recent increase in high-impact pivoting sports like volleyball, and a history of PCOS (which can predispose to metabolic stress) confirms this diagnosis. No further tests are required.
